overview:
Dr. Jodie Dionne is an Associate Professor of Medicine in the Division of Infectious Diseases and an Associate Professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology in the Division of Maternal-Fetal Medicine at UAB. She is Director of the Infection in Women and Pregnancy Research Program and Associate Director of Global Health in the UAB Center for Women's Reproductive Health. As a physician-scientist , Dr. Dionne designs and leads phase 1-4 clinical trials to identify new ways to treat and prevent infections in women and pregnancy. 

Dr. Dionne is also part of the leadership group of the NIH-funded Infectious Diseases Clinical Research Consortium (IDCRC) Network of Vaccine and Treatment Evaluation Units (VTEU),  chair of the World Health Organization/PAHO Regional Validation Committee for the Elimination of Mother to Child Transmission of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B (EMTCT+), and a member of the CDC/HRSA advisory committee on HIV, Viral Hepatitis and STD Prevention and Treatment. Dr. Dionne is also an active ID/HIV clinician and a teacher and mentor for research trainees in the US and abroad.
